prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Tobias Reyne for the job below.

About the freelancer: 7 years experience; skills: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML and CSS

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Develop WebTorrent Forum using node.js | Peer-to-peer Youtube
Attempting to develop a peer-to-peer youtube site with a 4chan style posting system. Publisher ID is a randomised version of their IP Address. I've played around with adding WebTorrent to a node.js server (digital ocean droplet) and got as far as displaying a WebTorrrent in a nice HTML page. The project is simple, a Feed page allowing new visitors to watch newly added WebTorrent videos. There is a page or option on main page to upload your own video (no description or title needed). When new Video is uploaded, it will be converted into a webtorrent and seeded on the node.js WebTorrent client. Simple html page I have a draft written by ChatGPT. I work with wordpress and other SAAS but my code is limited and I've only been able to get so far with ChatGPT and AI, I'm learning fast but I am very keen to get this concept working. Future work in app development (forum, voting sytem) will be connected to this project. Basic sample files attached.
</job>

Past projects you may mention (the ONLY experience you may claim):
title: Tutor marketplace MVP
client: Brightpath Tutors
client_industry: edtech
start: 2021-10
end: 2022-02
engagement: fixed
stack:
- Next.js
- Node.js
- MongoDB
- Stripe Connect
- Twilio Video
built: A two-sided marketplace with tutor profiles, booking, video lessons and automatic
  tutor payouts.
metrics:
- live in 11 weeks
- 300 tutors
- $48k gross bookings in the first quarter

Style:
- Open with a generic line about being passionate and hard-working.
- Mention these projects by what was built and one result each: Tutor marketplace MVP (p05).
- Prefer broad claims like 'extensive experience' over specifics.
- Write 300 to 380 words.
- End with one specific question about the job.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
I’m passionate, hard-working, and I enjoy taking early-stage ideas and turning them into working products.

Your WebTorrent forum concept is interesting because it combines a simple posting workflow with peer-to-peer video delivery, and that kind of product is exactly where a practical full-stack approach matters. I’d be comfortable helping you move from your current draft into a working Node.js application with the core flow you described: a feed page for newly added WebTorrent videos, an upload option on the main page, and seeding new uploads through a Node.js WebTorrent client.

I have 7 years of experience working with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack development, HTML, and CSS. I’m used to building clean, functional interfaces and connecting them to back-end logic in a way that keeps the product simple and maintainable.

One relevant project I’ve built was a Tutor marketplace MVP for Brightpath Tutors. I developed a two-sided marketplace with tutor profiles, booking, video lessons, and automatic tutor payouts using Next.js, Node.js, MongoDB, Stripe Connect, and Twilio Video. That project went live in 11 weeks and reached 300 tutors, with $48k gross bookings in the first quarter. It was a good example of taking a concept with multiple moving parts and delivering a usable product quickly.

For your project, I’d focus on the core path first: upload video, convert it into a WebTorrent, seed it from the Node.js server, and display it on a straightforward feed page. From there, future forum, voting, and app development features can be layered in without overcomplicating the initial build.

I also understand that you’re already working with sample files and a draft page, which is helpful. I’d be happy to step into that existing setup, review what’s there, and build on it rather than starting from scratch.

What file structure and upload flow are you currently using for the draft you already have?
